framework_findings.title: Citibank business fee schedule varies by state -- no single national figure is valid
framework_findings.detail: Citi maintains state-specific fee schedule PDFs (the one located during research was Texas-titled despite a separate 'NY schedule' reference existing elsewhere). Any fee figure recorded for Citibank must be tagged with the state it applies to, or it will misrepresent the actual account terms for institutions/persons in other states.
framework_findings.recommendation: Add a 'state' field alongside any Citibank (and potentially other multi-state-schedule banks) fee data point. Do not treat a single fetched Citi fee schedule as universally applicable.

framework_findings.title: Truist has two differently-dated fee schedule PDFs both indexed and surfaced by search
framework_findings.detail: One PDF is effective 2024-01-01 (stale), the other 2026-06-05 (current) -- both hosted on truist.com and both appeared in the same search pass. This is a concrete, observed instance of the exact risk the project's marketing-vs-official-fee-schedule verification step exists to catch, and it happened on the very first attempt to run that check against a bank beyond the original 12.
framework_findings.recommendation: The scraping pipeline should always parse and compare the stated 'effective date' on any fee schedule PDF before ingesting it, and should prefer the most recent when multiple versions of the same document type appear in search or on the same domain. This should be a standing rule in the automated Worker, not a manual one-off fix -- the same failure mode likely exists for other banks not yet checked.

framework_findings.title: A geo restriction can apply to financing products only, not deposit products, at the same institution
framework_findings.detail: NASA FCU restricts business credit cards and business loans to businesses located and operating in MD, VA, or DC (confirmed directly on their own Business Platinum Credit Card page). Their business checking, savings, money market, and certificate product pages carry no such restriction language. This means geo_restriction cannot be treated as one true/false value per institution -- it can be product-line-specific, and checking only the deposit-account pages (or only the financing pages) would miss half the picture.
framework_findings.recommendation: When researching geo_restriction going forward, check financing products (credit cards, loans) and deposit products (checking, savings, MM, certificates) separately rather than assuming a restriction found on one product type applies institution-wide. Consider whether geo_restriction needs a per-product-type sub-field rather than one institution-level value -- flagging this as a possible schema question for Kent rather than deciding it unilaterally (per rule 0.4).

framework_findings.title: Nominally geography/employer-restricted credit unions can be effectively nationwide via a sponsored association membership path
framework_findings.detail: Two institutions now confirmed with this pattern: Vibrant CU (any US citizen/permanent resident can join via a complimentary Illinois Consumer Council membership Vibrant itself enrolls you in and pays for) and NASA FCU (anyone can join via a complimentary one-year National Space Society membership if they do not otherwise qualify). In both cases the no-catch path is stated directly on the institution's own site, not inferred. This means membership_eligibility should never be marked as geographically/employer restricted based on the credit union's name or primary field-of-membership description alone -- the actual application/join page must be checked for one of these association-based catch-all paths before recording a restriction.
framework_findings.recommendation: When researching membership_eligibility for any credit union going forward (especially in Prompt C's 92-institution batch, several of which are employer/geography-named credit unions like Boeing Employees CU, SchoolsFirst FCU, Randolph-Brooks FCU), explicitly check the join/membership page for an association-based or donation-based catch-all eligibility path before concluding the institution is restricted. A name like 'NASA FCU' or 'Boeing Employees CU' is not sufficient evidence of a real restriction.

framework_findings.title: Eight institutions exist in both findata-research-intake-12-tagged.json and findata-research-top100-tagged.json, and the top-100 copy is stale relative to the intake-12 copy
framework_findings.detail: chartway-fcu, andrews-fcu, consumers-cu, service-cu, vibrant-cu, self-help-fcu, navy-federal-cu, and canyon-view-cu all appear in the top-100 list still marked research_status: identified_pending_url_registry with no source_urls -- but their intake-12 counterparts (chartway, andrews, consumers, service, vibrant, self-help, navyfederal, canyon-view) have been fully or partially researched through several Prompt A/B sessions, up to and including fully_verified account-level data. Running Prompt C on these 8 as if they were unresearched would duplicate real work and risk the two files drifting into different, possibly contradictory answers for the same institution.
framework_findings.recommendation: Before running Prompt C on any institution, cross-check its id against intake-12 first. For these 8, recommend copying the richer intake-12 data into the top-100 entry (or vice versa -- Kent should decide which file is the source of truth) rather than re-researching from scratch. Excluded these 8 from this session's Prompt C batch selection for that reason.
framework_findings.resolution_note: Resolved via a consolidation pass: all 8 overlapping institutions (chartway-fcu, andrews-fcu, consumers-cu, service-cu, vibrant-cu, self-help-fcu, navy-federal-cu, canyon-view-cu) had their top-100 placeholder entry replaced with the richer intake-12 research data, preserving the top-100 id and rank. The 4 intake-12 institutions with no top-100 counterpart (nasa, affinity-plus, four-leaf, cu1) were appended as supplementary entries (rank_in_100_list=null, supplementary_addition=true). findata-research-top100-tagged.json is now the single source of truth for all 20 researched institutions plus the 80 still-pending ones -- 104 total records. findata-research-intake-12-tagged.json can be considered superseded/archival going forward.

framework_findings.title: Comerica and Fifth Third Bank may now be the same combined entity
framework_findings.detail: While researching Comerica Bank, comerica.com itself displayed the banner 'Fifth Third Completes Merger with Comerica, Creating 9th Largest U.S. Bank.' Both Comerica and Fifth Third Bank already exist as SEPARATE entries in findata-research-top100-tagged.json, researched independently in different sessions (Fifth Third: session 2026-08-04 batch 2; Comerica: session 2026-08-04 batch 4) with different fee figures, different branch footprints, and different source URLs recorded. If the merger is complete, having two separate dataset entries risks presenting the same underlying institution twice with possibly-conflicting facts, or missing that a Kent-relevant answer from one brand now applies to both.
framework_findings.recommendation: Kent should decide whether to (a) merge these two entries into one record once the post-merger brand structure is confirmed (which name survives, are both brands operating in parallel for a transition period, etc.), or (b) keep them separate with an explicit cross-reference note in each record's research_notes, which is the interim approach taken this session. Recommend a quick news search on the merger's actual completion date and branding plan before the next research session touches either entry.

framework_findings.title: Digital FCU (DCU) and First Tech FCU have merged into a single credit union
framework_findings.detail: Confirmed via both dcu.org and US News: Digital Federal Credit Union and First Technology Federal Credit Union merged effective January 1, 2026, into a single credit union named First Technology Federal Credit Union, currently operating as two divisions (DCU and First Tech) during integration. Both institutions already exist as SEPARATE entries in findata-research-top100-tagged.json (digital-fcu-dcu and first-tech-fcu), researched independently in the same session with different fee figures, different branch footprints, and different source URLs. This is the second such merger finding in this project (see finding-comerica-fifth-third-merger) -- worth checking for a pattern of unannounced-to-this-project mergers among institutions researched from stale training data or aging third-party reviews.
framework_findings.recommendation: Same recommendation as the Comerica/Fifth Third finding: Kent should decide whether to merge these two entries into one record once the post-merger brand structure stabilizes, or keep them separate with explicit cross-reference notes (the interim approach taken this session). Given two mergers have now surfaced in one research project, consider adding a lightweight merger/acquisition check as a standard step in Prompt C for institutions that have not been touched in a while, rather than discovering it incidentally during unrelated fee research.

cybersecurity_scoring.recommendation: Hand off to the Worker pipeline (per Kent: already being built in a separate conversation). confirmations_2026-08-01.extended_cybersecurity_layers: Added 4 new externally-checkable fields to the cybersecurity_check schema (dnssec_status, email_auth_records [SPF/DKIM/DMARC], nameserver_redundancy, registrar_lock_status) based on https://dn.org/dns-security-best-practices-for-financial-institutions/ (DN.org, byline 'Staff', March 2025 -- itself a low-authority source on Harvard AUTHOR/CREDENTIALS, used here only as a checklist prompt, not cited as a primary authority). Deliberately excluded the article's internal-network-architecture recommendations (split-horizon DNS, SIEM log aggregation, recursive resolver ACLs, encrypted DNS for remote workers) since those describe how an institution runs its OWN network and aren't observable or relevant when evaluating whether a third-party institution's public URL is a trustworthy data source. All 4 new fields are defined but unpopulated -- same tooling gap as the original 5 layers, handed off to the Worker pipeline.

domain_scores_note: Lookup-only domain-level scoring registry (Option A, confirmed by Kent 2026-08-02). Any SourceUrl (institution-level or ranking_source) carries a 'domain' field; scoring lives ONCE here per domain, not duplicated per-URL. Rule: before scoring a new URL's Harvard/cybersecurity checks, look up its domain here first -- if already scored, reuse rather than re-score. Populated so far only from the 15 ranking_sources (11 distinct domains after dedup -- several ranking_sources share a domain, e.g. bankrate.com used for both bank and credit-union rankings). NO institution domain currently overlaps with a ranking_source domain, so no institution SourceUrl inherits a score yet -- this registry is ready to grow as institution source_urls get scored in future sessions, per Kent's new instruction that per-institution SourceUrl entries ARE now in scope for Harvard/cybersecurity scoring (voiding the 2026-07-31 scope-clarification note in findata-research-schema.md).
